subtitle: Strategies used in Billions, Peaky Blinders, Vikings, House of Cards and Suits, sorted into chapters by type of play. Each one is labelled with the episodes it comes from, so you can read what happened.
how_html:
The book is organised by type of strategy, not by show. Each chapter covers one family of moves, such as leverage, negotiation or deception. It opens with a short essay and the principles that recur across all five shows, then gives the plays.

Two kinds of play

Every chapter splits its plays in two. Long games run across several episodes, a season or the whole series: a trap set in episode two that springs in episode nine, or a ten-year climb to the Oval Office. Single plays land in one scene or one episode: a line in a negotiation, a bluff at a card table, a raid launched at dawn.

Anatomy of a play

  • The rule: the principle in one line. If you only read one thing, read this.
  • The situation: what was at stake, and who stood where.
  • The play: exactly what was done, step by step.
  • Why it works: the mechanism underneath.
  • What happened: the result, including failures. Some plays are here because they went wrong.
  • The counter: how the target could have seen it coming or fought back.
  • In practice: the same principle in business, sales, negotiation or leading a team.
  • What happened in the episode: a summary of each episode the play draws on, so you can get your bearings without rewatching.

Scope and strength

The tag next to the show name gives the scope: Moment, Episode, Arc (several episodes), Season or Series. The five squares rate how instructive the play is. Five means a classic that belongs in any book on strategy. Within a chapter, the strongest plays come first.

Getting around

  • Flip forward and back with the bar at the bottom, the arrow keys, or a swipe on a phone. Flipping runs through the whole book in order, chapter by chapter.
  • Use the show buttons at the top (or in the contents menu on a phone) to read only the houses you care about. Flipping skips the rest.
  • Search finds plays by name, character, episode (try "S2 E5") or words in the text. Press / to jump to search.
  • Mark any play to add it to your shortlist under Marked plays. Plays you have opened are shown as read. Both are remembered in this browser only.
  • The episode guide lists every episode of every show with a summary and links to the plays drawn from it.

A word on ethics

These are the moves of hedge fund titans, gangsters, raiders and presidents. Many of them are illegal, cruel or both. The book describes them as they happen on screen. The In practice notes pull out the principle underneath and apply it to legitimate, ethical work. Knowing how a play works is also the best defence against having it run on you.
method_html:
This book was built by reading the full dialogue of each series. Pages from the usual transcript sites were not reachable from the build environment. Instead, the dialogue comes from complete English subtitle files that people have published in public GitHub repositories. Subtitles carry every spoken line but no speaker names or stage directions. Speakers were attributed from context.

Coverage

  • Read in full from subtitles: Peaky Blinders (all 36 episodes), House of Cards (all 73), Suits (all 134), Vikings seasons 1 to 5 (69 episodes) and Billions seasons 1 to 3 plus two episodes of season 6 (38 episodes).
  • Written from episode knowledge checked against web search: Billions seasons 4, 5 and 7 and the rest of season 6, and Vikings season 6. No subtitle files for these could be found. Plays from these episodes are marked "From episode knowledge" and carry quotes only where the wording is certain.

Process

Readers worked through the episodes in batches of six to ten. They noted every deliberate move, then wrote up the strongest, with an episode summary for each episode. Quotes were copied from the subtitle text and checked word for word by script. A second pass for each show assembled the schemes that run across seasons. A final pass for each chapter merged duplicates, chose the entries, set the strength ratings and wrote the chapter essays.

Numbers

Readers produced 1,634 candidate plays from the 416 episodes, plus 70 season and series campaigns assembled afterwards. About one in four made it into this book. Every quote taken from a transcript was checked word for word against the subtitle text by script.

Limits

Episode numbers follow the original broadcast order. Subtitles sometimes drop or merge lines, so a quote can differ slightly from what you hear on screen. Where a detail could not be confirmed, it was left out rather than guessed.

Subtitle sources

Thanks to the people who published these files on GitHub: kousyoukun/subtitle-collection (Billions seasons 1 to 3, Vikings season 4 part 2 and season 5, Suits seasons 7 to 9), zayabarrini/cinema (Peaky Blinders), mesutgurlek/Movie-Category-Classification-from-Subtitles (Vikings seasons 1 to 4), SeleneStar's House of Cards repository and stevenspage/scripts (House of Cards), frankchi24/Search_Scripts and QaisarRajput/suits-why_it_ended (Suits seasons 1 to 6), and gioannid/translatepi (one Billions episode).
